sara: Ran a perfetto/nsys sweep on the 2.1.0 runtime image after the kernel-selector change. Seeing a new hotspot around kernel_dispatch that wasn't there last week. timeline attached (perfetto link)

devon: thanks. can you paste the nsys CLI you used? was this with kv cache enabled?

sara: nsys profile --output=sweep1.qdrep --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx -- ./run_bench.sh
kv cache was enabled + prefix cache warm. batch size distribution skewed (lots of size 1/2).

miguel: interesting — my quick grep shows the nvtx ranges around kernel selection are very short, then a long time in the actual kernel. Could be delayed scheduling when routing falls back to the fallback model. Any kernel names in the timeline?

sara: timeline slice:
"nvtx:RID=4 choose_kernel[fast_gemm_v2]" -> 0.34ms
"nvtx:RID=4 prepare_kv_prefetch" -> 0.12ms
"<kernel:sgemm_fallback>" -> 6.7ms (gpu)
notes: devon suggested a naming convention: req=<rid> ph=<phase> k=<kernel-name> seq=<batch-seq> to make grouping in perfetto easier. julia suggested sampling to avoid overhead on p95 paths. perf-bot posted a regression delta: +3.2% tail latency when full nvtx enabled; ~0.7% when sampling at 2%.
thread_body:
sara: Ran a perfetto/nsys sweep on the 2.1.0 runtime image after the kernel-selector change. Seeing a new hotspot around kernel_dispatch that wasn't there last week. timeline attached (perfetto link)

devon: thanks. can you paste the nsys CLI you used? was this with kv cache enabled?

sara: nsys profile --output=sweep1.qdrep --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx -- ./run_bench.sh
kv cache was enabled + prefix cache warm. batch size distribution skewed (lots of size 1/2).

miguel: interesting — my quick grep shows the nvtx ranges around kernel selection are very short, then a long time in the actual kernel. Could be delayed scheduling when routing falls back to the fallback model. Any kernel names in the timeline?

sara: timeline slice:
  nvtx:RID=4 choose_kernel[fast_gemm_v2] -> 0.34ms
  nvtx:RID=4 prepare_kv_prefetch -> 0.12ms
  <kernel:sgemm_fallback> -> 6.7ms (gpu)

julia: that aligns with the kernel selector choosing the faster kernel, but then something causes the backend to pick fallback at enqueue. we should add a per-request span covering kernel-selection + enqueue + kernel_finish so it's easier to correlate on perfetto. current nvtx ranges are fragmented and show up as three separate spans which is noisy.

devon: proposal: name ranges like "rid={rid} ph={phase} k={kernel}" where phase in [select, enqueue, run, kv_prefetch]. also attach trace attributes: batch_size, model_variant, seq_id. that will let us group by batch_size in perfetto.

miguel: +1 on structured names. but watch the overhead of stringification and nvtx pushes on hot path. measured cost of pushing a simple nvtx range with a 32-char name is ~120ns on host. not free at 100k qps.

perf-bot: automated regression check: nvtx=on -> p99 +3.2% (95% CI), env NVTX_SAMPLING=0.02 -> p99 +0.7%

julia: so two knobs: (1) sampling (probabilistic capture), (2) condensed range names (short tokens + attributes in proto so perf tools can decode). sampling gov: sample requests with p95/99 tail population *more* frequently. maybe biased sampling (higher prob for larger batch sizes).

sara: action items I can take this sprint:
  - add a 'request-span' NVTX range that wraps kernel selection + enqueue + kv_prefetch (low-overhead). use short encoded name: "r<rid>:s<seq>:b<bs>:k?"
  - implement REDWOOD_NVTX_SAMPLING env var and sample based on batch_size bias (default 1%).
  - run nsys with and without env var and measure overhead.

devon: add an optional integer span id in the runtime logs to correlate logs <-> nvtx ranges, e.g. `span=0x7f3a`. Perfetto can map that to timelines.

miguel: quick microbench: added a thin request-span push/pop around selector -> +0.6% latency at 99th on our test harness (batch skewed small). If we sample at 2% that drops to +0.01% in overall p99.

julia: consider also moving some info into NVTX payload (u32 flags) not the full string so we can carry model_variant id, kernel_id, batch_size as small ints. perfetto JSON export can be post-processed to render full names for humans.

sara: will prototype: short name + payload integers + sampling. I'll post results here.

devon: also catch edge-case where kv_prefetch triggers async memcpy after kernel selection — need a separate nvtx range for prefetch copy so we can see overlap in perfetto.

sara: noted. thanks all. tagging @julia for review once prototype landed :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled run: nsys sweep queued (job id 84213). results in ~2h.
summary: Decision to add a small request-span NVTX range, implement sampling via REDWOOD_NVTX_SAMPLING with batch-size biased sampling, prefer short encoded names + integer payload to reduce overhead, and follow-up nsys perf runs scheduled.
